correctness.rationale: Let B_j be disjoint triples of pendant vertices around t_(3j+2). Dominating these middle vertices forces at least m tail choices. Dominating cycle vertex c2 forces at least one cycle choice; equality m+1 would force c2 and t1, but t1 covers only two tail vertices, preventing m tail vertices from dominating all 3m tail vertices. The independent dominating set {c0,c2} union {t2,t5,...,t_(3m-1)} attains size m+2. Closed-neighborhood deletion of those middle tail vertices leaves C4, whose independence complex consists of two disjoint edges, with reduced integral H0=Z. Thus p=m+1 absent and p-q-1=0 nonzero. Sharp smallest n=7 unique is established by a finite exact integral Smith-form census of all 54 unlabeled unicyclic types of orders 3..7 with orbit-stabilizer labeled totals.

value.rationale: A natural open graph-family boundary from Berghoff Question 5.5 is resolved negatively for connected unicyclic graphs. An all-parameter structural counterexample plus exact first-order uniqueness gives an informative obstruction to extending a spectral-sequence vanishing criterion from paths and cycles; the finite classification is not a gratuitous arbitrary invariant.
